With GPT-5.5 as the frozen executor, Mastermind achieves an 84.5% pass rate, outperforming open-book PoC context (60.0%), Best-of-8 sampling (63.0%), and iterative improvement (77.0%). The same planner also improves GPT-5.4 mini and GLM~5.1 from 45.0% and 58.5% to 60.0% and 71.0%. These results demonstrate that learning high-level strategies is an effective and transferable mechanism for improving repository-scale SE agents.

AI.tldr: Mastermind introduces a dual-loop, strategy-centric framework for repository-scale vulnerability reproduction, achieving transferable high-level strategies that improve multiple LLM executors.
AI.motivation: Repository-level vulnerability reproduction is hard: agents must infer input grammars, craft PoCs, and verify patches; purely trajectory-based learning is brittle, so learning reusable strategies can generalize across tasks and executors.
AI.method: A dual-loop architecture where a trainable planner learns reusable vulnerability-reproduction strategies via supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and milestone-based GRPO; an experience loop maintains task-local strategy records guiding later attempts; the planner is trained independently of the executor to enable cross-executor transfer.
AI.result: Evaluated on CyberGym with 260 training tasks and 200 held-out tasks. With GPT-5.5 as the executor, Mastermind achieves 84.5% pass rate, outperforming open-book PoC context (60.0%), Best-of-8 sampling (63.0%), and iterative improvement (77.0%). The planner also improves GPT-5.4 mini from 45.0% to 60.0% and GLM-5.1 from 58.5% to 71.0%.
AI.conclusion: Learning high-level strategies yields effective and transferable improvements for repository-scale SE agents.

title: Learning Agile Intruder Interception using Differentiable Quadrotor Dynamics
summary: This paper presents a methodology for learning a control policy to intercept an intruder using the 3D direction unit vector to the intruder and the interceptor state. Prior deep reinforcement learning approaches assume either relative position or distance to the intruder is available, but this information is not readily accessible in real-world applications that employ passive, monocular camera sensors. Instead, we propose a solution that leverages an analytical policy gradient method using differentiable quadrotor dynamics to learn agile interception at speeds up to 10 m/s. The proposed approach outperforms baseline methods that utilize simplified point mass dynamics by an average of 30%.

AI.tldr: Uses a differentiable quadrotor dynamics model with an analytical policy gradient to learn interception using the 3D direction to the intruder and the interceptor state, suitable for monocular sensing. Outperforms simplified point-mass baselines by ~30% at speeds up to 10 m/s.
AI.motivation: Real-world monocular sensing missing reliable relative position/distance information; conventional DRL relies on such data. Need an approach that works with 3D direction cues and differentiable dynamics for agile, fast interception.
AI.method: Analytical policy gradient method leveraging differentiable quadrotor dynamics. Observations are the 3D direction unit vector to the intruder and the interceptor's state; training targets agile interception up to 10 m/s.
AI.result: The proposed method outperforms baselines that use simplified point-mass dynamics by an average of 30%.
AI.conclusion: A differentiable dynamics-based policy gradient framework with monocular cues can achieve agile interception performance, improving over simpler dynamic models and enabling feasible real-world deployment with passive sensors.

title: DeadPool: Resilient LLM Training with Hot-Swapping via Zero-Overhead Checkpoint
summary: State-of-the-art large language model (LLM) training takes tens of thousands of graphics processing units (GPUs) for months and encounters failures across the software and hardware stack. Existing fault-tolerance mechanisms either impose non-trivial overhead during failure-free execution or suffer from prolonged recovery latency, particularly under scenarios where a small subset of compute nodes experience permanent failures. %The tradeoff between failure-free overhead and recovery latency forms a space forms a Pareto frontier We present DeadPool to simultaneously address both optimization objectives. DeadPool incorporates a fault-tolerance mechanism that restores LLM training via hot-swapping, namely by replacing failed nodes with spare nodes without terminating the complete job. The hot-swapping of DeadPool is enabled by two ideas: First, it exploits an off-critical-path in-memory checkpointing mechanism for spatial redundancy. Second, it introduces a communicator reconstruction protocol that replaces failed nodes with spare nodes at runtime. DeadPool efficiently overlaps the in-memory checkpointing with computation, thus introducing zero overhead during error-free execution. Upon permanent node failures, DeadPool can rebuild memory states with minimal recomputation by leveraging in-memory checkpoints. We evaluate DeadPool across scales (up to 512 NVIDIA A100 GPUs) and LLMs (up to 65B parameters), and observe zero checkpoint overhead with hot-swapping recovery completing in under 40 seconds. These results show that DeadPool simultaneously achieves both zero-overhead error-free execution and extremely low recovery cost.

AI.tldr: DeadPool offers zero-overhead fault tolerance for large-scale LLM training by hot-swapping failed compute nodes with spare nodes using in-memory checkpointing and runtime communicator reconstruction, enabling sub-minute recovery with minimal recomputation.
AI.motivation: Large-scale LLM training requires thousands of GPUs and is vulnerable to software/hardware failures. Existing fault-tolerance either adds failure-free overhead or incurs long recovery latency, especially when a subset of nodes fail permanently. A method that minimizes both aspects would significantly improve efficiency and reliability.
AI.method: DeadPool introduces hot-swapping of failed nodes with spare nodes without terminating the job. It leverages off-critical-path in-memory checkpointing to create spatial redundancy and a runtime communicator reconstruction protocol to remap processes. The approach overlaps checkpointing with computation to achieve zero overhead during normal operation, and uses the in-memory checkpoints to rebuild memory states with minimal recomputation after permanent failures.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation up to 512 NVIDIA A100 GPUs and models up to 65B parameters shows zero overhead from checkpointing during failure-free execution and recovery times under 40 seconds for permanent failures.
AI.conclusion: DeadPool achieves both zero-overhead failure-free execution and very low recovery cost, effectively addressing the tradeoff between runtime overhead and fault-recovery latency in large-scale LLM training.

title: LASER: A Corrective Lens for LVLMs via Visual Attention Preservation and Sink Suppression
comment: The 19th European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV 2026)
summary: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) exhibit strong reasoning ability but suffer from visual forgetting during long-horizon decoding, where attention progressively drifts away from visual evidence. Existing methods largely treat this issue as a late-stage attention decay problem or attempt to mitigate it through heuristic reminders or post-hoc attention lifting. Through systematic empirical analysis, we find that performance degradation under visual forgetting is largely driven by two overlooked factors: early-stage attention decay disrupts evidence acquisition, and attention concentration on a subset of task-irrelevant visual sink tokens. Motivated by these insights, we propose LASER, a post-training framework that regulates both the visual attention trajectory and intra-visual token attention distribution during reasoning. Technically, LASER introduces two complementary rewards: a Visual Grounding Reward, which encourages the model to maintain attention on semantically salient visual tokens throughout decoding, and a Sink Suppression Reward, which penalizes excessive attention concentration on visual sink tokens. Together, these rewards preserve early-stage grounding while preventing attention collapse onto uninformative regions. Extensive experiments on eight benchmark datasets demonstrate that LASER consistently outperforms strong baselines, validating attention-aware training as an effective remedy for visual forgetting.

AI.tldr: LASER is a post-training framework for LVLMs that mitigates visual forgetting during long-horizon reasoning by regulating attention trajectories and intra-token focus. It uses two rewards—Visual Grounding and Sink Suppression—to maintain grounding on salient visual tokens and reduce attention to uninformative sink tokens, improving performance across eight benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Visual forgetting in large vision-language models arises from early-stage attention decay and over-reliance on a subset of visual sink tokens, leading to loss of visual grounding during decoding. Prior work treats it as a late-stage decay or uses heuristic reminders, but neglects how early evidence acquisition and token-level attention distribution contribute to forgetting.
AI.method: LASER is a post-training framework that adds two complementary rewards during reasoning: (1) Visual Grounding Reward to keep attention on semantically salient visual tokens throughout decoding, and (2) Sink Suppression Reward to penalize excessive attention on visual sink tokens. This jointly preserves early-stage grounding and prevents attention collapse.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation across eight benchmark datasets shows LASER consistently outperforms strong baselines, validating attention-aware training as an effective remedy for visual forgetting in LVLMs.
AI.conclusion: Attention-aware post-training with Visual Grounding and Sink Suppression rewards effectively mitigates visual forgetting by maintaining early visual grounding and avoiding attention collapse onto uninformative regions, with robust improvements across diverse datasets.

title: SimWorlds: A Multi-Agent System for Dynamic 3D Scene Creation
summary: LLM agents are increasingly used to translate natural language into 3D scenes in a procedural way, but existing systems focus on static output. Dynamic 4D scenes from text alone, in which liquids flow, particles emit, rigid bodies cascade, and articulated mechanisms move, remain largely unexplored despite their value as editable content and as physics-grounded training data for video generation and embodied AI. Two challenges set the dynamic case apart from static text-to-scene work: an agent must jointly coordinate spatial layout, multiple physics solvers, temporal sequencing, camera, and lighting in a single coherent scene, and verifying motion correctness from rendered video is fundamentally harder than judging a single image. We present SimWorlds: a multi-agent framework that produces dynamic, editable 4D scenes from text, with Blender-specific procedural knowledge, a planner-coder-reviewer workflow driving a fixed ordered sequence of construction stages, a layered scene protocol enforced by a deterministic verifier, and a runtime-state inspection tool suite that catches mechanism failures the rendered image cannot reveal. We also introduce 4DBuildBench, a benchmark for assessing both visual fidelity and physical consistency of the procedural dynamic 3D scenes generated from text prompts. Experiments show that SimWorlds outperforms prior dynamic Blender generation baselines.

AI.tldr: SimWorlds is a framework that generates dynamic 4D scenes from text by coordinating Blender-based procedures, planning, coding, reviewing, and verifying with a layered protocol and runtime tools; supported by 4DBuildBench benchmark, and it outperforms prior Blender-based dynamic generation baselines.
AI.motivation: There is a gap in text-to-dynamic-4D scene generation where motion, physics, and multi-subsystem coordination must be validated beyond a single image. A unified, editable, physics-grounded, and verifiable pipeline is needed for high-fidelity dynamic scenes and useful video data.
AI.method: Propose SimWorlds: a multi-agent framework with Blender-specific procedural knowledge, a planner–coder–reviewer workflow enforcing a fixed construction pipeline, a layered scene protocol with a deterministic verifier, and a runtime-state inspection toolset to detect mechanism failures unseen in rendered frames.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation shows SimWorlds achieves higher visual fidelity and physical consistency than prior dynamic Blender generation baselines, using 4DBuildBench to assess both aspects.
AI.conclusion: Dynamic text-to-4D scene generation is feasible with a structured, verifiable, and editable pipeline. The approach yields physics-grounded content suitable for animation, video generation training data, and subsequent embodied AI applications.

title: QuadRocket: An Aerial Robotic Testbed for Adaptive Thrust-Vector Control of Rocket-Like Vehicles
comment: Paper accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
summary: This paper presents QuadRocket, a quadrotor-based rocket prototype that provides a low-cost, low-risk platform for validating advanced thrust-vector control strategies for launch vehicle-type systems. The prototype consists of a cylindrical main body mounted on top of a quadrotor through a universal joint, forming a flying inverted pendulum with non-negligible inertia. For control design, the coupled system is modeled as a single axisymmetric rigid body actuated by a vectored force applied along its longitudinal axis. A reduced-attitude representation on the two sphere is adopted to explicitly exploit the vehicle's axial symmetry and to decouple yaw from the thrust-vector direction. On this model, we derive an adaptive backstepping controller that achieves almost global trajectory tracking in the presence of unknown constant disturbances, while a control-point transformation mitigates non minimum-phase behavior. The quadrotor is then treated as a thrust vector actuator, and a dynamic-surface-based attitude controller is designed to track the desired thrust-vector, accounting for actuation dynamics and avoiding explicit differentiation of virtual control signals. The complete architecture is evaluated in simulation and validated experimentally in an indoor motion-capture arena. Results demonstrate accurate trajectory tracking, effective disturbance compensation, and confirm the suitability of the QuadRocket as a versatile testbed for thrust-vector-controlled robotic vehicles.

AI.tldr: A low-cost quadrotor-mounted rocket prototype (QuadRocket) validates thrust-vector control strategies for launch-like systems using an axisymmetric rigid-body model, adaptive backstepping, and dynamic-surface attitude control; validated in simulation and indoor experiments.
AI.motivation: There is a need for a low-risk, affordable testbed to validate thrust-vector control concepts for launch-vehicle-type systems, and to exploit axial symmetry by decoupling yaw from thrust direction.
AI.method: Model the system as a single axisymmetric rigid body with thrust-vector actuation; use a reduced-attitude on the sphere to decouple yaw; derive an adaptive backstepping controller with a control-point transformation to mitigate non-minimum-phase behavior; implement a dynamic-surface-based attitude controller treating the quadrotor as a thrust-vector actuator while accounting for actuation dynamics and avoiding differentiation of virtual controls.
AI.result: Simulation demonstrates accurate trajectory tracking and disturbance rejection; indoor experimental validation confirms the controller’s effectiveness and the QuadRocket's suitability as a thrust-vector control testbed.
AI.conclusion: QuadRocket is a versatile, low-cost testbed for developing and validating thrust-vector-controlled robotic vehicles, capable of handling disturbances and enabling safe, rapid experimentation.

title: CALM: Interpretable Cross-Modal Alignment for Biomarker Discovery from Unpaired Data
summary: The interaction between brain structure and genetic influences is key to understanding neuropsychiatric disorders. However, most large-scale datasets are unimodal, providing either neuroimaging or genetics data. We propose CALM, a framework that learns interpretable associations between brain ROIs and genetic pathways from completely disjoint populations. CALM aligns the two modalities in a shared latent space via linear projections that simultaneously match the class-conditional latent distributions and ensure group separability. These projections provide interpretable pathway--ROI associations. When trained on unimodal imaging and genetics datasets, CALM generalizes to an unseen paired dataset, outperforming several state-of-the-art methods and ablation baselines. We also demonstrate stability of the learned associations against a paired baseline. Our experiments on autism spectrum disorder reveal immune and metabolic pathways linked to specific cortical regions and are consistent with established literature. Thus, CALM opens the door to leveraging large unimodal repositories for studying cross-modal interactions in brain disorders across disparate datasets.

AI.tldr: CALM enables cross-modal brain-imaging and genetics analysis from disjoint populations by learning a shared latent space with linear projections, yielding interpretable ROI–pathway associations and strong generalization to unseen paired data, demonstrated in autism.
AI.motivation: Large neuroimaging and genetic datasets are often unimodal and from separate cohorts. There is a need to integrate these modalities to understand brain-structure–genetic influences on neuropsychiatric disorders, even when paired data are unavailable.
AI.method: CALM uses linear projections to map each modality into a shared latent space, aligning class-conditional distributions and preserving group separability. The projections produce interpretable associations between brain ROIs and genetic pathways. The model generalizes from unimodal data to unseen paired datasets and is evaluated for stability against a baseline.
AI.result: CALM outperforms state-of-the-art methods and ablations on unimodal-imaging/genetics datasets, generalizes to unseen paired data, demonstrates stability, and identifies immune and metabolic pathways linked to specific cortical regions in autism, aligning with established literature.
AI.conclusion: CALM enables leveraging large unimodal repositories to study cross-modal brain–genetics interactions in neuropsychiatric disorders, providing interpretable ROI–pathway associations and broader cross-dataset generalization.

title: Consistent Scene Understanding in 3D Gaussian Splatting via Multi-Cue Mask Refinement
summary: Reliable instance-level scene understanding is a fundamental prerequisite for object-level interactions and high-fidelity 3D representations. While current methods often leverage 2D foundation segmentation models to obtain these priors, their 2D-centric design typically yields fragmented masks and inconsistent predictions across different views. To address these issues, we propose a novel framework that produces consistent 2D instance masks to guide the optimization of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) feature fields. Our framework consists of three main stages. (1) Multi-Cue Extraction that generates synergistic semantic, geometric, and structural priors from input images. (2) Multi-Cue-Guided Mask Merging process that consolidates fragmented masks using a composite merge score derived from semantic, depth, and edge cues. (3) Cross-View Mask Matching that establishes globally consistent identity assignments across all viewpoints. By transforming viewpoint-specific segments into coherent 3D primitives, our approach enables stable 3D instance segmentation and effective downstream editing tasks. Experiments demonstrate that our method significantly improves cross-view consistency and segmentation stability over existing baselines while maintaining high-fidelity photometric reconstruction.

AI.tldr: Three-stage framework integrates semantic, geometric, and structural cues to produce consistent 2D instance masks that guide 3D Gaussian Splatting, achieving improved cross-view consistency and stable 3D segmentation while preserving photometric reconstruction.
AI.motivation: Current 2D-centric instance segmentation leads to fragmented, view-dependent masks unsuitable for stable 3D understanding and editing; need cross-view consistent primitives for 3D scene representations.
AI.method: 1) Multi-Cue Extraction of semantic, geometric, structural priors; 2) Multi-Cue-Guided Mask Merging using a composite score from semantic, depth, and edge cues; 3) Cross-View Mask Matching to assign consistent identities across views and convert to 3D primitives, enabling 3DGS feature-field optimization.
AI.result: Empirical results show significant improvements in cross-view consistency and segmentation stability compared to baselines, while maintaining high-fidelity photometric reconstruction.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a unified, view-consistent 2D-to-3D mask pipeline that improves 3D instance segmentation and supports downstream editing tasks, without sacrificing reconstruction quality.

title: Repair the Amplifier, Not the Symptom: Stable World-Model Correction for Agent Rollouts
summary: As agent planning moves from short tool chains toward persistent workflows with thousands or tens of thousands of steps, failures will occur inside large planning graphs rather than in isolated predictions. Replanning the entire graph after every mistake is neither computationally realistic nor desirable: full-graph replay consumes large context budgets, exposes the LLM to many irrelevant symptoms, and can degrade long-context retrieval. This paper studies the missing component in such systems: a world-model corrector that repairs the failed planning graph in place. We compare two families of correctors. The first is the common engineering approach: scan nodes and edges, choose a suspicious local region, and ask an LLM to repair it. We implement strong engineering LLM correctors and find that they can help, especially when given very large contexts. The second family is our approach, WM-SAR (World-Model Subgraph Amplification Repair): instead of scanning for visible symptoms, it works backward from subgraph amplification, identifies the nodes and edges that keep re-amplifying error, and sends only that causal subgraph to the LLM. Across graph simulations and LLM repair experiments, WM-SAR substantially outperforms engineering correctors under realistic token budgets, achieves near-whole-graph stabilization with a compact region, and gives the LLM a cleaner repair target.

AI.tldr: WM-SAR is a world-model corrector that repairs planning graphs in place by tracing subgraph amplification. It outperforms engineering, local-region LLM repairers by sending a compact causal subgraph to the LLM, enabling near-whole-graph stabilization under realistic token budgets.
AI.motivation: As planning graphs scale to thousands of steps, failures occur inside the graph and full-graph replays are inefficient. A world-model corrector that repairs the graph in place is needed to maintain context and avoid irrelevant symptoms.
AI.method: Compare two corrector families: (1) engineering LLM correctors that scan local regions for repair; (2) WM-SAR that identifies nodes/edges that cause repeated amplification of errors by propagating backward from subgraph amplification and transmits only the causal subgraph to the LLM. Evaluated on graph simulations and LLM repair experiments under realistic token budgets.
AI.result: WM-SAR substantially outperforms engineering correctors, achieving near-whole-graph stabilization with a compact region and providing a cleaner repair target for the LLM.
AI.conclusion: Focusing on causal subgraphs that propagate error (subgraph amplification) is an effective strategy for large planning workflows, reducing context requirements and improving repair quality compared to local-region symptom-driven approaches.

title: Controllable Sim Agents with Behavior Latents
summary: Realistic traffic simulation requires agents that imitate logged behavior and can also be steered along interpretable axes. Such controllability enables engineers to isolate variables, reproduce specific edge cases, and test autonomous systems without real-world risk. We introduce Controllable Neural Variational Agents (CNeVA), a controllable simulated-agent framework that learns to infer a per-agent Gaussian behavior latent from per-channel discounted returns via a closed-form conjugate variational update, conditioning a rectified-flow trajectory generator trained on a mixed channel-mask curriculum for classifier-free guidance. To tackle scarcity in reward signals, we propose soft eligibility gates that replace hard binary thresholds with smooth exponential decay, preserving the gradient signal for near-threshold agents. On the Waymo Open Motion Dataset, CNeVA attains competitive realism on the benchmark while exposing per-channel controllability that the higher-ranked imitation models lack. Speed- and acceleration-based steering produces monotone responses without stall-induced reward hacking. Safety controllability is monotone and substantial with the introduction of soft eligibility. We manage to achieve steerable map compliance under a context-residual return measure. Furthermore, our experiment demonstrates that steering metrics must be read alongside physical-plausibility guardrails to avoid reward-hacking confounds.

AI.tldr: Introduces Controllable Neural Variational Agents (CNeVA) to produce realistic but steerable agent behavior by learning per-agent latent behavior from channel-wise returns and guiding a rectified-flow trajectory generator, with soft eligibility to maintain gradient signals. Evaluated on Waymo Open Motion with competitive realism and demonstrated per-channel controllability and safety monotonicity.
AI.motivation: Need for simulators that both imitate logged driving data and allow interpretable, controllable steering axes to test autonomous systems and study edge cases without real-world risk.
AI.method: Infer per-agent Gaussian latent from per-channel discounted returns via a closed-form conjugate variational update. Condition a rectified-flow trajectory generator trained with a mixed channel-mask curriculum for classifier-free guidance. Introduce soft eligibility gates to replace hard thresholds, preserving gradient signals.
AI.result: On Waymo Open Motion Dataset, CNeVA achieves competitive realism and exhibits per-channel controllability not present in higher-ranked imitators. Steering based on speed/acceleration yields monotone responses with no stall; safety controllability is monotone and enhanced by soft eligibility; steerable map compliance demonstrated under a context-residual return measure. Also show that steering metrics must be interpreted with physical-plausibility guardrails to avoid reward-hacking confounds.
AI.conclusion: CNeVA provides a viable framework for controllable, safe, and realistic simulation of driving agents, highlighting the interplay between controllability, reward signals, and guardrails; future work should address potential reward-hacking and broader generalization to diverse driving contexts.

title: Message Passing Based Two-Timescale Bayesian Learning for Joint Channel and Memory Hardware Impairments Tracking
summary: Hardware impairments in massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) receivers introduce inter-symbol memory and inter-element coupling, severely degrading channel estimation. This paper employs a residual recurrent gated unit (RGRU) to model the intra-slot memory of the hardware impairments and proposes a message-passing-based two-timescale Bayesian deep learning (MP-TTBDL) framework for joint channel and impairment tracking. Owing to small-scale fading, the wireless channel varies rapidly across slots, whereas hardware impairments drift slowly due to hardware aging and environmental variations. To capture these distinct physical timescales, a fastvarying Markov prior and a slow-varying Gaussian Markov prior are assigned to the sparse channel and the network parameters, respectively. Based on a multi-slot factor graph formulation, a message-passing algorithm is developed. Specifically, the inter-slot messages admit closed-form updates, while the intra-slot factor graph, due to its complex recurrent structure, is partitioned into a channel tracking module and an impairments calibration module. The channel tracking module performs sparse channel estimation via turbo orthogonal approximate message passing (Turbo-OAMP), and the impairments calibration module updates the impairment parameters via a specially designed deep approximate message passing (DAMP) procedure, with the two modules iteratively exchanging extrinsic information through expectation propagation (EP) until convergence. Simulation results show that the proposed framework robustly achieves lower channel estimation error than conventional compensators followed by channel estimation across different online impairment scenarios and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions.

AI.tldr: A two-timescale Bayesian deep learning approach combining residual recurrent gating (RGRU) for intra-slot hardware-memory and a Turbo-OAMP/DAMP two-module system to jointly track channels and impairments in massive MIMO; demonstrates improved channel estimation over baselines.
AI.motivation: Hardware impairments introduce inter-symbol memory and inter-element coupling in massive MIMO receivers, degrading channel estimation. A model capturing both fast-varying channels and slow-drifting impairments is needed for robust tracking.
AI.method: Model intra-slot impairment memory with a residual recurrent gated unit (RGRU). Use a multi-slot factor graph with fast-varying Markov prior for the channel and slow-varying Gaussian Markov prior for network parameters. Develop a two-module message-passing scheme: channel tracking via Turbo-OAMP and impairments calibration via a deep approximate message passing (DAMP) procedure. Exchange extrinsic information through expectation propagation (EP) until convergence.
AI.result: Simulation results show the proposed MP-TTBDL framework achieves lower channel estimation error than conventional compensators across various online impairment scenarios and SNR conditions.
AI.conclusion: The MP-TTBDL framework with RGRU-based impairment memory and two-module Turbo-OAMP/DAMP message passing effectively jointly track channels and calibrate impairments in massive MIMO under fast channel variations and slow impairment drift.

title: Beyond Pixel Diffs: Benchmarking Image Change Captioning for Web UI Visual Regression Testing
summary: Visual regression testing (VRT) is a standard quality assurance step in modern software release pipelines. On every change, it re-renders user interface (UI) screenshots, compares each one against an approved baseline image, and routes any detected difference to a human reviewer who decides whether it is an intended update or an unintended regression. A widely used approach, especially in open-source and continuous-integration pipelines, is pixel-level comparison, which is semantically blind and treats rendering noise and genuine defects identically, producing large volumes of false positives that force developers and testers to spend substantial time and effort manually reviewing flagged differences at every release cycle. Industry tools apply machine learning to VRT, but lack public evaluation. More critically, no dataset or benchmark exists to support natural language descriptions of UI changes, a capability that tells testers what changed in words instead of leaving them to interpret a binary flag or a highlighted region. To address the gap, we propose a new task, Web UI Image Change Captioning (WUICC), which sits at the intersection of VRT and image difference captioning (IDC), and release WUICC-bench, its first dataset and benchmark for the task. We evaluate eleven representative IDC methods, together with two zero-shot general-purpose LLMs. We find that: (1) these methods tend to struggle in the Web UI domain due to its layout diversity, dense text, and fine-grained changes, and (2) yet the trained methods already suppress non-meaningful visual noise far more selectively than the pixel-level comparison VRT relies on, providing a solid foundation for future domain-specific research.

AI.tldr: Introduces Web UI Image Change Captioning (WUICC) and WUICC-bench as a dataset/benchmark for describing UI changes, bridging visual regression testing (VRT) and image difference captioning (IDC); evaluates multiple IDC methods and zero-shot LLMs, showing domain challenges but potential for reducing non-meaningful visual noise compared to pixel-level VRT.
AI.motivation: Pixel-level VRT treats rendering noise and real defects the same, causing many false positives in web UI with diverse layouts and dense text; there was no public benchmark for natural language descriptions of UI changes, hindering evaluation and progress.
AI.method: Define the WUICC task and assemble WUICC-bench, a Web UI image-diff captioning dataset; benchmark 11 IDC methods plus 2 zero-shot LLMs on the dataset; analyze performance across layout diversity, text density, and fine-grained changes.
AI.result: IDC methods struggle in the Web UI domain due to layout diversity and fine-grained changes; nevertheless, trained IDC methods suppress non-meaningful visual noise more selectively than pixel-level VRT, suggesting a promising foundation for domain-specific improvements.
AI.conclusion: WUICC-bench provides a realistic benchmark for evaluating natural-language descriptions of UI changes and motivates future research in UI-aware captioning and hybrid VRT approaches that combine visual and linguistic signals.

title: Verifiable Knowledge Expansion through Retrieval-Grounded Formal Concept Analysis
comment: 8 pages, 2 figures, Accepted to the 8th epiDAMIK ACM SIGKDD International Workshop on Epidemiology meets Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery (epiDAMIK 2026)
summary: Ontology construction requires deciding which objects, attributes, and structural relations should be accepted as valid knowledge. Language models can propose such structures from text, but their outputs can still be unsupported or inconsistent. This paper proposes a retrieval-augmented small language model (SLM) framework that uses formal concept analysis (FCA) as a symbolic verification loop for knowledge expansion. Starting from seed attributes, FCA proposes implications over a growing formal context. A retrieval-grounded SLM oracle then validates each implication or returns a counterexample. The oracle also supports incidence judgments, consistency checks, and attribute proposals, making accepted implications, counterexamples, contradictions, and corrections inspectable. In a rare ataxia setting constructed from Orphadata resources, retrieval-grounded 10-seed runs obtain relation F1 of 0.29-0.52 and closure-based implication F1 of 0.22-0.30. Larger seed sets increase the number of evaluated implications and often improve implication F1. The lower implication scores reflect a stricter evaluation of derived implications, where one missed or extra relation can affect several implication judgments. Ablations show that incidence judgments in a fixed object-attribute setting can improve closure-based implication scores. However, identifying positive object-attribute pairs remains difficult even when the candidate objects and attributes are fixed.

AI.tldr: Retrieval-augmented SLM with a symbolic FCA verification loop for ontology expansion; FCA-derived implications are validated by a retrieval-based oracle, yielding inspectable results with modest F1 on a domain-specific dataset; larger seed sets increase evaluated implications but stringent evaluation lowers scores, with positive object-attribute pair identification remaining challenging.
AI.motivation: To combine neural language models with symbolic formal concept analysis to produce verifiable, inspectable ontology knowledge and reduce unsupported or inconsistent outputs.
AI.method: A small language model augmented with retrieval; commence from seed attributes; FCA derives implications over a growing formal context; a retrieval-grounded SLM oracle validates each implication or returns a counterexample; oracle also performs incidence judgments, consistency checks, and proposes attributes; outputs include accepted implications, counterexamples, contradictions, and corrections; experiments conducted in a rare ataxia setting built from Orphadata, with 10-seed runs and various seed sizes, reporting relation F1 and closure-based implication F1.
AI.result: Relation F1 ranges from 0.29 to 0.52; closure-based implication F1 ranges from 0.22 to 0.30; larger seed sets increase the number of evaluated implications and can improve implication F1; lower scores reflect strict evaluation where a single misclassification can affect several implications; ablations show incidence judgments in a fixed object-attribute setting can improve closure-based implication scores; identifying positive object–attribute pairs remains difficult even with fixed candidate objects/attributes.
AI.conclusion: The approach yields inspectable, verifiable inferences and benefits from incidence judgments, but overall implication quality is limited by strict evaluation and the challenge of discovering valid positive object–attribute pairs; future work should target better positive pair discovery and more robust evaluation strategies.

title: Embodied.cpp: A Portable Inference Runtime of Embodied AI Models on Heterogeneous Robots
summary: Embodied AI models now span vision-language-action (VLA) models and world-action models (WAMs), but practical deployment remains fragmented across model-specific Python stacks, backend assumptions, and robot-side glue code, especially on heterogeneous edge devices. Existing inference runtimes are designed mainly for request-response serving and therefore do not satisfy the runtime contract of embodied deployment: multi-rate execution inside closed-loop control, latency-first batch-1 inference on heterogeneous hardware, and extensible embodied interfaces beyond fixed token I/O. We present Embodied.cpp, a portable C++ inference runtime for embodied models. Based on an architectural analysis of representative VLA models and WAMs, Embodied.cpp captures a shared execution path and organizes it into five layers: input adapters, sequence builders, backbone execution, head plugins, and deployment adapters. The runtime provides modular multi-rate execution, latency-first fused inference, and extensible operator and I/O support, enabling deployment across heterogeneous devices, robots, and simulators through one backend abstraction. We evaluate Embodied.cpp on two VLA models, HY-VLA and pi0.5, and on a preliminary WAM benchmark using a LingBot-VA Transformer block. The VLA deployments achieve successful closed-loop execution with 100.0% and 91.0% task success rates, respectively. The WAM benchmark reduces block memory from 312.2 MiB to 88.1 MiB. These results show that Embodied.cpp improves deployment efficiency while preserving high accuracy across diverse embodied model architectures.

AI.tldr: Proposes Embodied.cpp, a portable C++ runtime for embodied AI models enabling multi-rate, latency-first, extensible execution across heterogeneous devices; shows gains in memory and task success across VLA and WAM benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Fragmented deployment landscape for embodied AI (vision-language-action and world-action models). Existing runtimes are oriented to request-response and do not satisfy multi-rate, latency-prioritized, closed-loop embodied deployment across heterogeneous hardware. A unified runtime would streamline deployment and improve efficiency.
AI.method: Architectural analysis of representative VLA (HY-VLA, pi0.5) and WAM models; design a five-layer runtime (input adapters, sequence builders, backbone execution, head plugins, deployment adapters); implement modular multi-rate execution, latency-first fused inference, and extensible operator/I/O support; provide a backend abstraction to deploy on diverse devices, robots, and simulators.
AI.result: Evaluations on two VLA models (HY-VLA, pi0.5) and a preliminary WAM benchmark (LingBot-VA Transformer block) show: VLA deployments achieve 100.0% and 91.0% task success; WAM benchmark memory reduced from 312.2 MiB to 88.1 MiB, indicating deployment efficiency gains.
AI.conclusion: Embodied.cpp facilitates deployment across diverse embodied model architectures with improved efficiency while preserving accuracy, through a portable, multi-rate, latency-first runtime with extensible interfaces.

title: Revisiting Decentralized Online Convex Optimization with Compressed Communication
summary: Decentralized online convex optimization (D-OCO) is a popular framework for distributed applications with streaming data. To tackle the communication bottleneck, previous studies have investigated D-OCO with compressed communication and proposed several algorithms that are variants of online gradient descent (OGD). However, for D-OCO with exact communication, the best existing algorithms are variants of follow-the-regularized-leader (FTRL). In this paper, for the first time, we propose two FTRL-type algorithms for D-OCO with compressed communication. Compared with OGD-type algorithms, our algorithms are more elegant in both algorithmic design and theoretical analysis. The key insight is that the dual update mechanism of FTRL allows us to make a simple application of the technique for average consensus with communication compression. More specifically, our first algorithm considers the full-information setting, and can match the existing regret bounds. Our second algorithm is designed for the bandit setting, and can significantly improve both the regret bounds and communication costs of existing algorithms.

AI.tldr: Introduces two FTRL-type D-OCO algorithms with compressed communication (full-information and bandit); matches or improves regret bounds and reduces communication costs, via dual updates enabling consensus with compression.
AI.motivation: Address the communication bottleneck in decentralized online convex optimization (D-OCO) and extend FTRL advantages to compressed settings, providing elegant design and analysis beyond OGD-based methods.
AI.method: Propose two FTRL-type algorithms for D-OCO with compressed communication; leverage dual update mechanics to apply average consensus with compression; first algorithm in full-information setting, second in bandit setting.
AI.result: Full-information variant matches existing regret bounds; bandit variant significantly improves both regret bounds and communication costs compared to prior algorithms.
AI.conclusion: FTRL-based approach yields elegant, effective algorithms for D-OCO with compression, with notable gains in the bandit setting and a clean dual-update perspective for consensus under communication constraints.

title: ReQuest: Rethinking-based Question-Aware Frame Selection for Long-Form Video QA
summary: Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have substantially advanced video understanding, yet long-form video QA remains challenging under fixed input token budgets, where uniform sampling can be inefficient for evidence localization. We propose ReQuest , an uncertainty-driven, question-adaptive keyframe selection pipeline that aligns question intent with relevant video content through selective computation. ReQuest integrates (i) a lightweight question-aware selector distilled from MLLM-generated supervision, (ii) Re-thinking Routing that triggers additional inference only when the model is uncertain with a length-adaptive criterion, and (iii) uncertainty-guided adaptive non-maximum suppression that selects temporally diverse frames while adjusting spacing based on question difficulty. As a plug-andplay method, ReQuest improves long-video QA without modifying or fine-tuning the underlying MLLM. Experiments on Video-MME, MLVU, and LongVideoBench demonstrate consistent accuracy gains with competitive computational cost, with particularly strong improvements in medium and long video regimes.

AI.tldr: Uncertainty-driven, question-adaptive keyframe selection (ReQuest) improves long-form video QA by selectively computing on relevant frames without fine-tuning the base MLLM.
AI.motivation: Long-form video QA under fixed input token budgets struggles to locate evidence; uniform sampling is inefficient for evidence localization. A question-aware, adaptive computation strategy can focus processing on content pertinent to the query.
AI.method: A plug-and-play pipeline with three components: (i) a lightweight, question-aware selector distilled from MLLM supervision, (ii) Re-thinking Routing that triggers extra inference only when the model is uncertain using a length-adaptive criterion, and (iii) uncertainty-guided adaptive non-maximum suppression to select temporally diverse frames with spacing adjusted by question difficulty.
AI.result: Consistent accuracy gains on Video-MME, MLVU, and LongVideoBench with competitive computational costs; particularly strong improvements for medium and long video regimes.
AI.conclusion: ReQuest enables improved long-video QA without modifying or fine-tuning the underlying MLLM, demonstrating effective evidence localization and efficient selective computation across datasets.

title: Subliminal Clocks: Latent Time Modelling in Diffusion Language Models
comment: Equal contribution: Thomas Fontanari and Simone Petruzzi
summary: Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) have recently emerged as a promising alternative to autoregressive models. Unlike standard diffusion-based approaches, DLMs are not explicitly conditioned on a timestep, raising a natural question: do these models internally represent denoising progress, and how is such information used downstream? In this work, we show that DLMs do in fact encode a latent representation related to the diffusion timestep within their residual streams. We find that this signal can be reliably extracted using probes across layers, indicating that denoising progress is decodable from internal activations. We further demonstrate that steering the model along a low-dimensional subspace associated with the inferred timestep allows us to systematically modulate its notion of denoising progress, leading to predictable changes in model confidence and entropy. Finally, we analyse the geometry of the identified representation, showing that it exhibits structured and interpretable properties in activation space, and shedding light on how such a signal is processed by these models.

AI.tldr: DLMs encode a decodable latent denoising-progress signal in their residual streams; steering this signal modulates model confidence and entropy.
AI.motivation: Understand internal representations in non-timestep-conditioned diffusion language models and whether denoising progress information is decodable and usable for control.
AI.method: Probe internal activations across layers to extract the latent signal and assess decodability; manipulate along a low-dimensional subspace aligned with the inferred timestep; measure effects on model confidence and entropy; analyze the geometry of the activation-space representation.
AI.result: The latent signal is reliably decodable across layers; steering along the inferred-timestep subspace yields predictable changes in perceived denoising progress, confidence, and entropy; the representation exhibits structured, interpretable geometry in activation space.
AI.conclusion: DLMs maintain an internal, manipulable notion of denoising progress, informing our understanding of diffusion-based generation and enabling controlled manipulation of model behavior.

title: VT-WAM: Visual-Tactile World Action Model for Contact-Rich Manipulation
summary: Contact-rich manipulation requires policies to react to local deformation, pressure, slip, and friction, yet these cues are temporally sparse and often invisible in visual observations. Existing visual-tactile policies usually feed tactile observations directly into action prediction, but rarely model tactile deformation dynamics during action generation. In this paper, we introduce VT-WAM, a Visual-Tactile World Action Model that jointly learns future visual prediction, tactile deformation prediction, and action prediction within a unified flow matching framework. In particular, VT-WAM introduces (1) Asymmetric Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) attention to bridge a first-frame visual anchor with temporal tactile dynamics, and (2) contact-gated Action-Visual-Tactile Attention Guidance (AVTAG) to encourage action queries to rely on tactile evidence during contact phases. Across six real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks, VT-WAM achieves a 71.67% average success rate, outperforming Fast-WAM by 26.67% and OmniVTLA by 35.84%. Ablations demonstrate that modeling tactile deformation dynamics and guiding contact-phase tactile attention are both important for contact-rich tasks. Project website: https://vt-wam.github.io/.

AI.tldr: A unified Visual-Tactile World Action Model (VT-WAM) predicts future visuals, tactile deformation, and actions within a flow-matching framework, using asymmetric Mixture-of-Transformers attention and contact-gated AVTAG to leverage tactile cues during contact. It achieves state-of-the-art performance on six real-world contact-rich tasks, outperforming Fast-WAM and OmniVTLA, with ablations confirming the importance of modeling tactile dynamics and tactile-guided attention.
AI.motivation: Visual-tactile policies typically rely on visual data and often ignore or underutilize tactile deformation dynamics, especially during contact. There is a need to bridge a visual anchor with temporal tactile signals to better predict action in contact-rich manipulation.
AI.method: VT-WAM integrates future visual, tactile deformation, and action predictions inside a unified flow-matching framework. It introduces (1) Asymmetric Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) attention to connect a first-frame visual anchor with temporal tactile dynamics, and (2) contact-gated Action-Visual-Tactile Attention Guidance (AVTAG) to bias action queries toward tactile evidence during contact. The model is evaluated on six real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks.
AI.result: Average success rate of 71.67% across six tasks; outperforms Fast-WAM by 26.67 percentage points and OmniVTLA by 35.84 percentage points. Ablations show the importance of modeling tactile deformation dynamics and contact-phase tactile attention.
AI.conclusion: Modeling tactile deformation dynamics and guiding attention with tactile evidence during contact phases materially improves performance in contact-rich manipulation, demonstrating the effectiveness of VT-WAM and its specialized attention mechanisms for integrating vision, touch, and action.

title: UniWind: Toward Unified Day-Ahead Wind Power Forecasting via Physics-Informed State Routing
summary: Day-ahead wind power forecasting is essential for cost-effective power-system operation. It is primarily driven by future meteorological conditions while retaining temporal dependencies in power generation. In practice, observed wind-farm power often entangles physically available power with local environmental effects and latent operational states, such as shutdowns and curtailment. Existing physical models provide useful constraints but adapt poorly across wind farms, whereas data-driven models can capture rich correlations but often conflate meteorological effects with state-induced deviations. In this study, we propose UniWind, a wind power forecasting model based on physics-informed state routing. UniWind first employs a Physical Prior Estimator to construct a site-calibrated physical prior by combining site-conditioned monotonic warping with a shared physical power curve. It further applies a physical upper-bound constraint to shape this prior as a soft envelope of available wind power generation. UniWind then proposes a Latent State Encoder to model operating-state embeddings and transforms the physical prior into final power forecasts through a State-aware Power Corrector, which uses knowledge-guided supervised state routing and bounded, state-specific expert correction. Full-shot and cross-farm zero-shot experiments on more than 20 real-world datasets demonstrate the accuracy and robustness of UniWind.

AI.tldr: UniWind uses physics-informed state routing to improve day-ahead wind power forecasts by combining a site-calibrated physical prior with latent state embeddings, achieving accurate and robust predictions across multiple wind farms, including zero-shot cross-farm scenarios.
AI.motivation: Physical models are not easily transferable across wind farms; data-driven models may conflate meteorological signals with operational states; there is a need to separate meteorological effects from state-induced deviations to improve generalization.
AI.method: Physical Prior Estimator builds a site-calibrated prior via site-conditioned monotonic warping and a shared physical power curve, plus a soft upper-bound constraint forming an envelope of available wind power. Latent State Encoder learns operating-state embeddings. State-aware Power Corrector uses knowledge-guided supervised state routing and bounded, state-specific expert correction to turn the prior into final forecasts.
AI.result: Full-shot and cross-farm zero-shot experiments on more than 20 real-world datasets demonstrate UniWind's accuracy and robustness.
AI.conclusion: Integrating physics-informed priors with state routing yields transferable, accurate wind power forecasts and robust performance across wind farms.

title: InterCMDM: Block-Causal Diffusion for Autoregressive Human Interaction Generation
comment: Accepted to ECCV 2026, Project website: https://yu1ut.com/InterCMDM-HP/
summary: Text-conditioned human interaction generation must capture both long-range temporal causality within each individual and tightly coupled coordination between partners. Existing interaction diffusion models typically denoise full sequences using bidirectional attention, which obscures causality and hinders streaming and long-horizon generation. Autoregressive alternatives enforce causality but often suffer from temporal drift, leading to coordination degradation and unstable interaction dynamics over time. We propose InterCMDM, a block-causal latent diffusion framework for autoregressive two-person interaction generation. InterCMDM introduces a Dual-Stream Causal Diffusion Transformer that maintains separate causal streams for each person while modeling inter-person dependencies via unified dual-stream attention with multi-task attention masks. These masks unify interaction modeling within a single attention mechanism and support diverse coordination behaviors, including simultaneous actions, reactive responses, leader-follower dynamics, and independent motion. By training a single model across these mask configurations as a form of data augmentation, InterCMDM enables controllable interaction generation by simply selecting the desired attention mask at inference time. Finally, a block-wise diffusion objective enables stable latent rollout over long sequences without repeated decode-encode cycles. InterCMDM achieves state-of-the-art performance on InterHuman and Inter-X, improving text-motion alignment, realism, and long-horizon continuity.

AI.tldr: A block-causal latent diffusion model (InterCMDM) for autoregressive two-person interaction generation, using a dual-stream causal transformer and mask-based attention to enable controllable, long-horizon, stable interactions.
AI.motivation: Existing interaction diffusion methods either use bidirectional denoising, which harms causality and streaming, or autoregressive methods that suffer temporal drift and degraded coordination. A need exists for long-horizon, controllable, text-conditioned two-person interactions.
AI.method: Proposes Dual-Stream Causal Diffusion Transformer with separate causal streams for each person and unified dual-stream attention guided by multi-task attention masks. Masks enable diverse coordination (simultaneous actions, reactive responses, leader-follower, independent motion). Training across mask configurations acts as data augmentation. A block-wise diffusion objective enables stable latent rollout for long sequences without repeated decode-encode cycles.
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on InterHuman and Inter-X, with improvements in text-motion alignment, realism, and long-horizon continuity.
AI.conclusion: InterCMDM provides a flexible, controllable framework for text-conditioned two-person interaction generation. Mask-based attention supports various coordination behaviors within a single model, and the block-wise diffusion objective ensures stable long-range generation.

title: Safety Testing LLM Agents at Scale: From Risk Discovery to Evidence-Grounded Verification
summary: LLM agents increasingly perform autonomous actions through external tools, leading to complex and evolving safety risks. However, existing safety testing targets expert-designed safety violations, and the corresponding outcomes are evaluated by hard-coded rules, making them costly to extend as agents evolve. To this end, we present Vera, an end-to-end automated safety testing framework that instantiates software engineering testing principles for non-deterministic agents through a three-stage, self-reinforcing pipeline. First, a literature-driven exploration continuously discovers and structures emerging risks into taxonomies of safety risks, attack methods, and tool execution environments. Second, combinatorial composition across taxonomy dimensions produces executable safety cases, each specifying a concrete safety goal, a programmatically constructed initial state, and a deterministic verification predicate grounded in observable artifacts. Third, adaptive execution runs heterogeneous agents in isolated sandboxes where a control agent steers multi-turn interaction based on runtime observations, while evidence-grounded verifiers judge outcomes from environment state and tool-call evidence rather than model self-report. We evaluate Vera on four production agent frameworks (OpenClaw, Hermes, Codex, Claude Code), revealing substantial safety weaknesses, with average attack success rates reaching 93.9\% under multi-channel attacks; we also release Vera-Bench, comprising 1600 executable safety cases spanning 124 risk categories across three execution settings. These results indicate that modular, executable testing infrastructure is essential for rigorous and maintainable safety evaluation of rapidly evolving agentic systems at scale. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/Yunhao-Feng/Vera.

AI.tldr: Vera is an end-to-end automated safety testing framework for non-deterministic LLM agents, using a three-stage pipeline (taxonomy-driven risk discovery, combinatorial executable safety case generation, and adaptive sandboxed execution with evidence-based verifiers). It reveals safety weaknesses across multiple agent frameworks, with Vera-Bench providing 1600 executable safety cases; code is open-source.
AI.motivation: Current safety testing focuses on expert-designed violations with hard-coded rules and does not scale as agentic systems evolve and rely on external tools. A scalable, automated testing framework is needed to continuously evaluate and improve safety in evolving agents.
AI.method: Three-stage pipeline: (1) literature-driven exploration to build taxonomies of safety risks, attack methods, and tool environments; (2) combinatorial composition across taxonomy dimensions to create executable safety cases with concrete goals, initial states, and deterministic verification predicates based on observable artifacts; (3) adaptive execution in isolated sandboxes where a control agent manages multi-turn interaction and verifiers assess outcomes from environment state and tool-call evidence instead of self-reports.
AI.result: Evaluation on four production agent frameworks (OpenClaw, Hermes, Codex, Claude Code) shows substantial safety weaknesses, with an average attack success rate of 93.9% under multi-channel attacks. Vera-Bench contains 1600 executable safety cases across 124 risk categories in three execution settings. Code is publicly available.
AI.conclusion: A modular, executable testing infrastructure is essential for rigorous and scalable safety evaluation of rapidly evolving agentic systems; Vera enables maintainable, end-to-end safety testing at scale.

title: SCAPE: Accurate and Efficient LLM Training with Extreme Sparse Communication
summary: Communication increasingly dominates the cost of Large Language Model (LLM) pre-training, especially under data-parallel and sharded training schemes, where gradient synchronization and parameter reconstruction overhead increase with model size and system scale. Existing communication-reduction methods either sparsify raw gradients, which can be unstable for modern Adam-style optimizers at high sparsity, or quantize communication, whose savings are fundamentally bounded by bit width and often incur additional runtime overhead. We present SCAPE, a communication-efficient distributed optimizer for LLM training that exploits the stability of AdamS's first-moment to enable aggressive sparsification without loss of LLM quality. Instead of constructing masks from raw gradients, SCAPE derives them from first-moment-based statistics, partitions mask generation across workers to align with optimizer sharding, and delays mask usage by one step so that mask synchronization can overlap with computation. SCAPE also reconstructs the quantities required for second-moment updates from a single synchronized sparse buffer, avoiding an additional collective. We implement SCAPE in Megatron-LM and evaluate its convergence by pre-training GPT-345M on OpenWebText and Llama-500M on SlimPajama-6B using 32 NVIDIA GH200 GPUs on TACC Vista. In both models, SCAPE preserves training stability, validation loss, and downstream task accuracy under 90\% and 99\% sparsity. For Llama-500M, SCAPE reduces end-to-end pre-training wall-clock time by up to 43.3\% while maintaining model quality comparable to dense AdamW and AdamS. For Llama-1.8B, SCAPE achieves up to 3.26$\times$ speedup per step compared to dense AdamS.

AI.tldr: SCAPE is a communication-efficient distributed optimizer for LLM pre-training that uses first-moment-based sparsification and overlap-enabled scheduling to maintain stability and speedups at high sparsity without extra communication.
AI.motivation: Communication overhead dominates LLM pre-training in data-parallel/sharded regimes. Existing sparsification/quantization either destabilizes Adam-style optimizers or hits a fundamental bit-width bound with added runtime costs. A sparsification method that preserves optimizer stability and overlaps communication is needed.
AI.method: SCAPE derives sparsification masks from first-moment statistics rather than raw gradients, partitions mask generation across workers to align with optimizer sharding, delays mask usage by one step to enable overlap with computation, and reconstructs second-moment updates from a single synchronized sparse buffer to avoid extra collectives. Implemented in Megatron-LM and evaluated on GPT-345M/OpenWebText and Llama-500M/SlimPajama-6B with 32 NVIDIA GH200 GPUs; comparisons against dense AdamW/AdamS.
AI.result: SCAPE maintains training stability, validation loss, and downstream accuracy under 90% and 99% sparsity. It reduces end-to-end pre-training time by up to 43.3% for Llama-500M and achieves up to 3.26x per-step speedup for Llama-1.8B compared with dense AdamS.
AI.conclusion: SCAPE demonstrates that AdamS-based sparse optimization can be aggressively sparsified and overlapped with computation to achieve substantial speedups in large-scale LLM pretraining without sacrificing model quality.

title: RTE-FM-Dehazer: Radiative Transfer Equation Inspired Flow Matching for Real-World Image Dehazing
summary: Single-image dehazing aims to recover a clear scene from a hazy image and is generally formulated as an image-to-image translation task; however, it faces two limitations. Its performance depends heavily on the haze-formation priors embedded in the model. Prevailing methods adopt the Atmospheric Scattering Model (ASM), whose assumptions of single scattering and homogeneous media are often violated, leading to residual haze and color drift. Moreover, large-scale real hazy/clear pairs are impractical to collect, and existing synthesis approaches fail to reproduce the full complexity of natural haze. To address these issues, we present RTE-FM-Dehazer, a novel dehazing approach, together with a scalable data pipeline. Unlike the ASM, the Radiative Transfer Equation (RTE) jointly accounts for both scattering and absorption, naturally accommodating the non-homogeneous, multiple-scattering media that characterize real hazy scenes. Motivated by the structural similarity between the RTE diffusion-absorption term and the ODE in flow matching, we introduce a diffusion-absorption regularizer derived from a reduced RTE, to steer the flow matching trajectory at each step. Next, leveraging modern vision-language models, we build an automated pipeline and release P-HAZE, a dataset of 50000 realistic hazy/clear pairs. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that RTE-FM-Dehazer, trained solely on P-HAZE, effectively eliminates artifacts like residual haze and color drift, exhibits strong cross-domain generalization, and achieves leading results on five real-world dehazing benchmarks.

AI.tldr: A radiative-transfer-based dehazing framework (RTE-FM-Dehazer) with a diffusion-absorption regularizer and a 50k-pair hazy/clear dataset (P-HAZE) yields better artifact removal, cross-domain generalization, and state-of-the-art results on real benchmarks.
AI.motivation: The Atmospheric Scattering Model (ASM) assumptions (single scattering, homogeneous media) often fail in real hazy scenes, causing residual haze and color drift; lack of scalable, realistic hazy/clear data hampers learning-based dehazing; a physics-grounded, scalable data pipeline is needed.
AI.method: Replace ASM with the Radiative Transfer Equation (RTE) to model scattering and absorption in non-homogeneous, multi-scattering media. Introduce a diffusion-absorption regularizer derived from a reduced RTE to guide the diffusion/flow-matching trajectory. Build an automated pipeline leveraging vision-language models to synthesize a large, realistic hazy/clear dataset (P-HAZE) of 50,000 pairs.
AI.result: RTE-FM-Dehazer, trained solely on P-HAZE, effectively suppresses residual haze and color drift, exhibits strong cross-domain generalization, and achieves leading performance on five real-world dehazing benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: The physics-grounded RTE approach, together with a scalable P-HAZE dataset, improves dehazing quality and generalization over ASM-based methods. The data pipeline mitigates data scarcity, though computational complexity and reliance on RTE approximations may warrant further investigation.

title: MMIR-TCM: Memory-Integrated Multimodal Inference and Retrieval for TCM Clinical Decision Support
summary: Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) diagnosis, particularly through tongue inspection, faces persistent challenges in subjectivity and reproducibility. The application of multimodal artificial intelligence to TCM clinical tasks, such as syndrome differentiation and prescription generation, is significantly hampered by the semantic gap between visual tongue features and textual reasoning, as well as the lack of large-scale, standardized datasets. To address these challenges, we introduce MMIR-TCM, a novel framework that emulates the diagnostic process of TCM experts by integrating multimodal large language model(MLLM) with memory-augmented segmentation and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Employing a three-stage architecture, MMIR-TCM integrates a training-free Memory-SAM module for robust tongue extraction, a fine-tuned Qwen3-VL model for structured tongue diagnosis generation, and a Qwen3-based RAG component for evidence-grounded clinical decision support generation. The framework was developed and validated using MedTCM, a new large-scale multimodal dataset that we introduce specifically for advanced TCM research. To properly evaluate our framework's clinical accuracy, which existing metrics fail to capture, we also developed TDEU, a domain-specific evaluation metric incorporating semantic understanding and diagnostic importance. Our comprehensive experiments demonstrate that MMIR-TCM significantly outperforms leading models, including GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 Flash.

AI.tldr: MMIR-TCM: a multimodal LLM-based framework that fuses memory-augmented segmentation and retrieval-augmented generation for tongue-diagnosis in Traditional Chinese Medicine, validated on a new MedTCM dataset with a domain-specific metric (TDEU), and outperforming GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 Flash.
AI.motivation: Subjectivity and poor reproducibility in tongue diagnosis; semantic gap between visual tongue features and textual reasoning; scarcity of large, standardized multimodal datasets for TCM AI.
AI.method: Three-stage architecture: (1) Memory-SAM for training-free tongue extraction; (2) fine-tuned Qwen3-VL for structured tongue-diagnosis generation; (3) Qwen3-based RAG for evidence-grounded decision support. Introduces MedTCM as a large-scale multimodal dataset and TDEU as a domain-specific evaluation metric.
AI.result: MMIR-TCM significantly outperforms leading models (including GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 Flash) in comprehensive experiments.
AI.conclusion: MMIR-TCM effectively emulates a TCM expert’s diagnostic workflow by integrating multimodal perception, structured reasoning, and evidence-grounded generation; it establishes MedTCM and TDEU as resources to advance advanced TCM AI research.

title: DL-VINS-Factory: A Modular Framework for Learned Visual Front-Ends in Visual-Inertial SLAM
summary: Deep-learning features excel in visual matching, yet their practical value in tightly coupled visual-inertial SLAM (VI-SLAM) remains insufficiently characterized. We present DL-VINS-Factory, a unified framework that integrates learned feature extractors (ALIKED, RaCo, SuperPoint, XFeat) with either Lucas--Kanade (LK) optical-flow tracking or LightGlue (LG) descriptor matching. All front-ends share a sliding-window Ceres back-end, with optional AnyLoc DINOv2-VLAD loop closure, and 4-DoF pose-graph optimization. We benchmark the system across the four datasets covering indoor, unstructured outdoor, aggressive-motion, and visually degraded conditions. Results show that learned front-ends are viable for real-time embedded VI-SLAM, but are not universally superior to classical tracking. Relative to the corresponding GFTT+LK baseline, ALIKED+LG reduces EuRoC ATE by $5\%$ in monocular odometry and by $7\%$ in stereo with loop-closure. On NTU-VIRAL, where aggressive aerial motion increases inter-frame viewpoint change, ALIKED+LG stereo reduces loop-closed ATE by $12\%$. In Botanic Garden dataset, optical-flow tracking remains preferable, but learned keypoints still improve over the baseline GFTT, in which SuperPoint+LK reduces grayscale camera ATE by $29\%$, while RaCo+LK reduces RGB camera ATE by $38\%$. On SubT-MRS, learned front-ends display varying degree of improvement based on individual cases. With TensorRT acceleration on a Jetson AGX Orin, all valid configurations run in real time between $29$--$47$ FPS in monocular mode and $18$--$33$ FPS in stereo mode for the EuRoC and NTU-VIRAL datasets. AnyLoc further confirms roughly $2$--$7\times$ more valid loops than BRIEF+DBoW2. The implementation is open-sourced at https://github.com/limshoonkit/DL-VINS-Factory-ROS2/.

AI.tldr: A unified DL-VINS-Factory framework integrates learned feature extractors with either LK tracking or LightGlue descriptor matching for VI-SLAM, evaluated across diverse datasets with real-time performance and mixed gains over classical baselines; open-source release.
AI.motivation: To systematically assess the practical value of deep-learning-based feature front-ends in tightly-coupled visual-inertial SLAM and to provide a flexible, comparable framework for benchmarking different front-ends under a real-time VI-SLAM pipeline.
AI.method: Integrates learned feature extractors (ALIKED, RaCo, SuperPoint, XFeat) with LK optical-flow or LightGlue matching, all feeding a sliding-window Ceres back-end with optional AnyLoc DINOv2-VLAD loop closure and 4-DoF pose-graph optimization; TensorRT-accelerated on Jetson AGX Orin; evaluated on four datasets (EuRoC, NTU-VIRAL, Botanic Garden, SubT-MRS) under various conditions; open-source implementation.
AI.result: Learned front-ends are viable for real-time VI-SLAM but not universally superior to GFTT+LK baselines. Specific improvements include ALIKED+LG reducing EuRoC monocular ATE by 5% and stereo by 7% with loop closure; NTU-VIRAL stereo loop-closed ATE reduced by 12%; Botanic Garden shows mixed results with SuperPoint+LK reducing grayscale ATE by 29% and RaCo+LK reducing RGB ATE by 38%; SubT-MRS results vary by case; TensorRT yields 29–47 FPS monocular and 18–33 FPS stereo on EuRoC/NTU-VIRAL; AnyLoc increases valid loops by roughly 2–7x over BRIEF+DBoW2.
AI.conclusion: The framework demonstrates practicality of learned front-ends in real-time VI-SLAM with dataset- and method-dependent gains; offers a flexible, open-source platform for benchmarking front-ends; limitations include dataset-specific performance and the 4-DoF optimization choice which may affect generalizability to full 6-DoF VI-SLAM.

title: WARP: Weight-Space Analysis for Recovering Training Data Portfolios
comment: This work appears in the ICML 2026 Workshop on Weight-Space Symmetries (WSS): from Foundations to Practical Applications. Our source code is available at github.com/SprocketLab/WARP
summary: Foundation models are routinely released to the public, yet the data recipes used to train them -- such as domain mixture weights that determine how different sources are sampled -- are rarely disclosed. This creates an access asymmetry: researchers study the resulting models but lack visibility into the training distribution that produces them. Prior works for inferring training data, such as membership inference, detect at the level of individual samples and thus cannot characterize the global composition of the training corpus. We introduce WARP, a framework that recovers a fine-tuned model's training mixtures directly from its released weights. WARP interpolates between the base and fine-tuned models using model merging, generating pseudo-checkpoints that approximate the missing training trajectory and expose a geometric footprint of the training data in the weight space. From these simulated footprints, WARP extracts geometric features and maps them to domain proportions using either a parameter-free softmax readout or an MLP projector trained on synthetic mixtures. In controlled experiments with BERT and GPT-2, WARP recovers domain mixtures with an average MAE as low as 0.046 and 0.104 respectively, outperforming membership inference and a variant with access to the true training trajectory.

AI.tldr: WARP recovers the training data mixtures (domain proportions) used to fine-tune a model by simulating its training trajectory through model merging, then mapping geometric footprints in weight space to mixture proportions, enabling global data-distribution auditing from released weights.
AI.motivation: Foundation models are released with undisclosed data sources. Global training distribution (domain mixture) is hidden, unlike sample-level leakage methods; this limits transparency and reproducibility in evaluating training data influence.
AI.method: Compute pseudo-checkpoints by merging base and fine-tuned models to interpolate the training trajectory. Extract geometric features from the weight space of these merged models and map them to domain proportions via a parameter-free softmax readout or an MLP trained on synthetic mixtures.
AI.result: On BERT and GPT-2, WARP recovers domain mixtures with mean absolute error as low as 0.046 (BERT) and 0.104 (GPT-2), outperforming membership inference and a baseline using the true trajectory.
AI.conclusion: WARP provides a practical, model-weight–based method to audit and quantify the global training data composition of fine-tuned foundation models, revealing a latent geometric footprint of training mixtures.

title: MedStreamBench: A Time-Aware Benchmark for Streaming and Proactive Medical Video Understanding
summary: Existing medical video benchmarks primarily evaluate whether a model produces the correct answer, but rarely assess whether it answers at the right time. In real clinical settings, AI systems must decide not only what to predict, but also when to answer, defer judgment, or proactively raise alerts. This creates a critical gap between benchmark evaluation and deployment requirements. We present MedStreamBench, a benchmark for time-aware medical video understanding. MedStreamBench integrates 22 medical datasets and 5,419 QA instances across four temporal settings: retrospective, present, future, and proactive. Unlike conventional benchmarks that assume full-video access, MedStreamBench restricts models to temporally bounded evidence windows and supports both single-turn and streaming evaluation. We further introduce a proactive monitoring setting that requires models to determine whether and when clinically relevant alerts should be triggered. Beyond answer correctness, MedStreamBench evaluates temporal behavior through responsiveness and post-evidence stability. Experiments on leading general-purpose and medical vision-language models reveal a substantial gap between offline recognition and temporally grounded decision-making, with performance dropping markedly in streaming and proactive settings. Our benchmark is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/Venn2024/MedStreamBench.

AI.tldr: A time-aware benchmark (MedStreamBench) for medical video understanding evaluates not only accuracy but also when to answer, including streaming and proactive alerting, revealing a gap between offline recognition and temporally grounded decision-making.
AI.motivation: Existing medical video benchmarks focus on correctness with full-video access; deployment requires timely decisions and proactive alerts, which are under-evaluated in current benchmarks.
AI.method: MedStreamBench integrates 22 medical datasets and 5,419 QA instances across four temporal settings (retrospective, present, future, proactive); restricts models to temporally bounded evidence windows; supports single-turn and streaming evaluation; introduces proactive monitoring; includes metrics for responsiveness and post-evidence stability; openly available on HuggingFace.
