AI.result: Empirical results show nearly an 8-fold increase in accuracy over the base model on 360° visual search tasks, plus significantly improved exploration efficiency, establishing a new state-of-the-art.
AI.conclusion: EAGLE-360 demonstrates that leveraging global priors and topology-aware encodings can effectively guide embodied 360° visual search, enabling robust, efficient exploration and superior performance, aided by a large panoptic dataset and a tailored training regime.

title: Combating Textual Noise and Redundancy: Entropy-Aware Dense Visual Token Pruning
summary: Visual token pruning is a crucial strategy for accelerating VLMs by compressing redundant image patches, yet existing methods often fail to preserve critical cues under dense instructions and fine-grained queries. In this paper, we investigate this failure and identify two underlying bottlenecks: the widespread dispersion of textual noise that corrupts dense cross-modal scoring, and the feature fragmentation inherent to standard token selection. To address these issues, we propose Entropy-Aware Dense Pruning (EADP), a framework that reformulates pruning as a structured compression problem. EADP first leverages statistical entropy to quantify and filter out textual noise, yielding a robust, fine-grained instruction relevance score. Subsequently, instead of naive Top-K selection, EADP casts token selection as a submodular maximization problem with a spatial prior, explicitly ensuring a holistic and non-redundant visual representation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EADP improves the accuracy-efficiency trade-off of VLMs, robustly preserving fine-grained visual cues under strict token budgets while achieving SoTA performance on challenging multimodal benchmarks.

AI.tldr: Entropy-Aware Dense Pruning (EADP) improves VLMs by filtering textual noise via entropy and guiding token selection with a submodular, spatially-aware objective to ensure non-redundant, holistic visual representations under tight budgets.
AI.motivation: Dense cross-modal scoring is easily corrupted by textual noise and feature fragmentation in standard pruning, hindering fine-grained instruction alignment and efficient, robust VLMs.
AI.method: A two-stage approach: (1) entropy-based filtering to quantify and remove textual noise, producing a robust, fine-grained instruction relevance score; (2) token selection framed as submodular maximization with a spatial prior, replacing simple Top-K to yield holistic, non-redundant visual patches.
AI.result: Empirical results indicate improved accuracy-efficiency trade-offs, robust preservation of fine-grained visual cues under strict token budgets, and state-of-the-art performance on challenging multimodal benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Recasting pruning as structured compression with entropy-aware filtering and submodular, spatially-informed selection mitigates textual noise and feature fragmentation, delivering efficient and accurate VLMs.

title: GeoMix: Descriptor-Free Visual Localization via Global Context and Multi-Detector Training
summary: Descriptor-free visual localization eliminates high-dimensional descriptor storage, preserves scene privacy, and simplifies map maintenance, yet its accuracy still lags far behind descriptor-based pipelines. We identify this gap to insufficient geometric discriminability in geometry-only matching. Without visual appearance, current methods underutilize local geometry cues, lack the global context among keypoints, and overfit to a single keypoint detector. We further observe that descriptor-free matching naturally enables multi-detector training, as heterogeneous keypoints can be optimized in a shared geometry-only space without aligning descriptor spaces. Building on these insights, we propose GeoMix, a descriptor-free 2D-3D matching framework that strengthens geometric discriminability at three levels. Locally, directional and distance-aware embeddings enrich neighborhood aggregation with fine-grained spatial structure. Globally, learnable context nodes aggregate and redistribute scene-wide information via cross-attention to resolve ambiguities beyond local receptive fields. At the training level, Mix-Training exploits this detector-agnostic geometry space to learn representations across multiple keypoint detectors. Extensive experiments on MegaDepth, Cambridge Landmarks, 7Scenes, and Aachen Day-Night show that GeoMix sets a new state of the art among descriptor-free methods, reducing 75th-percentile rotation error by 89\% and translation error by up to 90\% over the previous best, while generalizing zero-shot to unseen detectors and narrowing the gap to descriptor-based pipelines. Code is available at $\href{https://github.com/YejunZhang/Geomix}{\text{this links}}$.

AI.tldr: GeoMix introduces a descriptor-free 2D-3D matching framework that enhances geometric discriminability locally and globally, and enables detector-agnostic multi-detector training. It achieves state-of-the-art results among descriptor-free methods and narrows the gap to descriptor-based pipelines, with strong zero-shot generalization.
AI.motivation: Descriptor-free localization lags descriptor-based methods due to limited geometric discriminability and reliance on a single keypoint detector. There is an opportunity to exploit local geometry cues, global context, and multi-detector training to improve accuracy while preserving privacy.
AI.method: GeoMix strengthens geometric discriminability at three levels: (1) locally with directional and distance-aware embeddings for neighborhood aggregation; (2) globally via learnable context nodes and cross-attention to fuse scene-wide information; (3) during training with Mix-Training to learn detector-agnostic representations across multiple keypoint detectors.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on MegaDepth, Cambridge Landmarks, 7Scenes, and Aachen Day-Night show GeoMix achieves new state-of-the-art among descriptor-free methods, with substantial reductions in 75th-percentile rotation error (up to 89%) and translation error (up to 90%) over prior descriptor-free methods, and zero-shot generalization to unseen detectors, while narrowing the gap to descriptor-based pipelines.
AI.conclusion: GeoMix demonstrates that multi-level geometric discriminability and detector-agnostic training can surpass existing descriptor-free approaches and approach descriptor-based localization performance, offering strong privacy and maintenance advantages; code is publicly available.

title: Towards Robustness against Typographic Attack with Training-free Concept Localization
comment: 15 pages main text, provisionally accepted to ECCV 2026
summary: Models trained via Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP) serve as the foundational vision encoders for most modern Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs). Despite their widespread adoption, CLIP models exhibit a critical yet underexplored failure mode: irrelevant text appearing within images confounds visual representations, biasing them toward lexical meaning rather than true visual semantics. This robustness issue, commonly described as a Typographic Attack (TA), exposes a vulnerability that poses a significant risk to safety-critical applications such as autonomous driving. To achieve interpretable and effective robustness against TA, we propose a novel, training-free mechanistic interpretability method. Our method provides sampling-based interpretations of hidden state representations and quantitatively attributes semantic versus lexical focus to individual attention heads. Through probabilistic analysis and circuit mining, we isolate specific Vision Transformer (ViT) components that disproportionately encode lexical information, thereby identifying the mechanistic source of TA. We further show that simple interventions applied directly to the identified circuits, without any additional training, can substantially improve robustness against Typographic Attacks in object classification. These interventions, such as selective adjustment of attention weights, also outperform both supervised and training-free defense methods. Our experiments demonstrate that applying the proposed intervention to the vision encoders of several state-of-the-art LVLMs yields substantial gains in Visual Question Answering accuracy under Typographic Attack interference on RIO-Bench. These results confirm both the efficacy and the generalizability of our mechanistic approach. Code is released at https://github.com/Liu-524/SamplingTAR.

AI.tldr: A training-free mechanistic interpretability method identifies and mitigates Typographic Attacks (TA) on CLIP-like vision encoders by sampling hidden-state representations to quantify semantic vs lexical focus across ViT attention heads; targeted circuit-level interventions (adjusting attention) improve robustness, outperforming supervised and training-free defenses, with demonstrated gains in LVLM QA tasks under TA.
AI.motivation: CLIP-based vision encoders are vulnerable to irrelevant text (Typographic Attacks) that biases representations toward lexical cues, risking safety-critical applications. There is a need for interpretable, training-free robustness methods that pinpoint mechanistic sources of TA and provide effective defenses.
AI.method: Use sampling-based interpretability to obtain hidden-state representations and attribute attention heads to semantic vs lexical focus. Apply probabilistic analysis and circuit mining to locate ViT components disproportionately encoding lexical information. Implement simple, training-free interventions directly on identified circuits (e.g., selective adjustment of attention weights) to reduce lexical bias.
AI.result: Interventions yield substantial robustness gains against Typographic Attacks in object classification and VQA, outperforming both supervised and other training-free defenses. Effects generalize across state-of-the-art LVLMs and improve Visual Question Answering accuracy under TA on RIO-Bench. Code for the method is released.
AI.conclusion: A training-free, mechanistic approach can identify the lexical-information bottlenecks in CLIP-based vision encoders and provide effective, generalizable defenses against Typographic Attacks by targeted circuit-level interventions in ViT architectures.

title: Seek to Segment: Active Perception for Panoramic Referring Segmentation
summary: Existing referring segmentation models passively process static images captured from fixed perspectives, limiting their applicability in Embodied AI, where agents must perform active perception in the continuous 360$^\circ$ environments. To bridge this gap, we introduce a novel task: Active Panoramic Referring Segmentation (APRS). In this setting, an agent is required to adjust its viewing direction ($Δθ, Δφ$) to explore the 360$^\circ$ environment, seeking the object specified by a user instruction for segmentation. To tackle this challenging task, we propose PanoSeeker, a memory-augmented agent for efficient APRS. Rather than relying on heuristic scanning, PanoSeeker integrates a Vision-Language Model (VLM) with EgoSphere, an explicit spatial visual memory. By progressively integrating sequential local observations into a unified 360$^\circ$ representation, EgoSphere enables the agent to plan efficient and non-redundant search trajectories. Once the target is found, the agent performs active viewpoint alignment and outputs the segmentation mask. Furthermore, we curate an expert-annotated search trajectory dataset with memory timelines for Supervised Fine-Tuning, followed by Reinforcement Learning post-training to explicitly optimize PanoSeeker's exploration efficiency. Extensive experiments on our newly established APRS benchmark demonstrate that PanoSeeker achieves superior search efficiency and segmentation accuracy, significantly outperforming adapted state-of-the-art baselines.

AI.tldr: Introduces Active Panoramic Referring Segmentation (APRS) and PanoSeeker, a memory-augmented agent that uses EgoSphere and a Vision-Language Model (VLM) to actively explore 360° environments for referring segmentation; includes an expert trajectory dataset and RL fine-tuning, achieving improved search efficiency and segmentation accuracy over baselines.
AI.motivation: Addresses the gap in current referring segmentation, which is confined to static images, by enabling active perception and exploration in continuous 360° spaces relevant to Embodied AI.
AI.method: PanoSeeker combines a Vision-Language Model with EgoSphere, an explicit spatial visual memory that incrementally fuses local observations into a unified 360° representation. The agent plans non-redundant search trajectories, performs active viewpoint alignment upon locating the target, and outputs a segmentation mask. A curated expert-annotated search trajectory dataset with memory timelines supports Supervised Fine-Tuning, followed by Reinforcement Learning to optimize exploration efficiency.
AI.result: Experiments on a newly established APRS benchmark show superior search efficiency and segmentation accuracy, outperforming adapted state-of-the-art baselines.
AI.conclusion: The work advances active perception for panoramic referring segmentation by integrating memory-augmented perception and vision-language guidance; the annotated trajectory dataset and RL training further enhance exploration efficiency and performance, suggesting strong potential for embodied AI tasks.

title: From SRA to Self-Flow: Data Augmentation or Self-Supervision?
summary: Representation alignment has become an effective way to accelerate diffusion transformer training and improve generation quality. Recent self-alignment methods, such as SRA and Self-Flow, further remove the dependency on external pretrained encoders by constructing alignment within the diffusion model itself. However, the mechanism behind the improvement from SRA to Self-Flow, dual-time scheduling, remains under-examined: Self-Flow attributes its gain to interactions between tokens at different noise levels, where cleaner tokens help infer noisier ones. In this work, we revisit this explanation and ask whether the gain instead comes from data augmentation along the noise dimension. To disentangle these factors, we introduce Attention Separation, which preserves the same dual-timestep input as Self-Flow while blocking attention between tokens assigned to different noise levels. Surprisingly, removing such interaction does not degrade performance and can even improve it, suggesting that the improvement from SRA to Self-Flow mainly comes from data augmentation. Furthermore,We show that Attention Separation itself provides an augmentation effect by splitting a single image into multiple effective training parts to expand the training data. Based on these observations, we combine self-representation alignment with dual-timestep and attention-separation augmentation, and demonstrate the effectiveness of this design on ImageNet.

AI.tldr: Attention Separation analysis reveals that SRA→Self-Flow gains in diffusion transformers stem primarily from data augmentation along the noise dimension, not inter-token interactions; attention separation can itself augment data by splitting an image into multiple training parts; combining self-representation alignment with dual-timestep and attention separation improves ImageNet performance.
AI.motivation: To disentangle the mechanisms behind performance gains from self-representation alignment methods (SRA vs Self-Flow) in diffusion models, specifically whether token-level interactions across noise levels or data augmentation along the noise axis drives the improvement.
AI.method: Introduce Attention Separation by preserving the same dual-timestep input as Self-Flow while blocking attention between tokens assigned to different noise levels. Evaluate the impact of removing cross-noise interactions. Demonstrate that Attention Separation provides augmentation by splitting a single image into multiple training parts. Combine self-representation alignment with dual-timestep and attention-separation augmentation.
AI.result: Removing cross-noise attention does not degrade performance and can improve it, indicating data augmentation along the noise dimension is the primary source of gains. Attention Separation itself yields augmentation by effectively creating multiple training instances from one image. The combined design improves diffusion training on ImageNet.
AI.conclusion: The observed gains from SRA to Self-Flow primarily stem from data augmentation along the noise axis rather than cross-token interactions. Attention Separation serves as a complementary augmentation, and integrating self-representation alignment with dual-timestep scheduling and attention-separation augmentation yields improved performance on ImageNet.

title: PointDiT: Pixel-Space Diffusion for Monocular Geometry Estimation
summary: State-of-the-art single-image 3D reconstruction methods often rely on complex hybrid architectures and loss functions, or compress geometry into latent spaces in order to leverage pre-trained latent diffusion models. In this work, we show that such architectural overhead and intricate loss formulations are unnecessary. We introduce a minimalist pixel-space Diffusion Transformer, built on a plain ViT, that operates directly on raw 3D point map patches and is conditioned on image tokens from a pre-trained DINOv3. Unlike existing latent diffusion approaches, we train our diffusion backbone entirely from scratch, eliminating the need for point map tokenizers. Despite its simplicity, our approach surpasses complex latent-based diffusion models while remaining significantly simpler than hybrid alternatives. Notably, it produces sharper geometric structure and is more robust in highly ambiguous regions, such as transparent objects.

AI.tldr: A minimalist pixel-space diffusion transformer (ViT) operates directly on raw 3D point map patches, conditioned on image tokens from a pre-trained DINOv3, trained from scratch, outperforming latent diffusion models with a simpler architecture and yielding sharper geometry and greater robustness in ambiguous regions.
AI.motivation: Eliminate architectural overhead and intricate loss formulations of existing single-image 3D reconstruction methods by avoiding latent diffusion and point-map tokenizers, while leveraging pre-trained image representations.
AI.method: A pixel-space diffusion transformer built on a plain ViT; directly processes raw 3D point map patches (no tokenizers); conditioning on image tokens from a fixed pre-trained DINOv3; diffusion backbone trained from scratch.
AI.result: Outperforms complex latent-based diffusion models; produces sharper geometric structure; more robust in highly ambiguous regions such as transparent objects; simpler than hybrid approaches.
AI.conclusion: A minimal, end-to-end train-from-scratch pixel-space diffusion transformer suffices for high-quality 3D reconstruction, challenging the necessity of latent diffusion or elaborate hybrid architectures.

title: Alignment Is All You Need For X-to-4D Generation
summary: Generative diffusion models excel at synthesizing high-quality images, videos, and 3D content under multimodal control. However, arbitrary user-defined modality-to-4D (X-to-4D) generation remains challenging due to the high cost of constructing diverse datasets and the limited scalability of existing methods. This paper presents Align4D, a flexible framework that translates any-modal input into coherent video-3D pairs, using video to guide 4D motion and 3D data to shape 4D geometry. Align4D introduces three key techniques: (1) Object Distance Alignment, which searches Video-Aligned and Multiview-Aligned Object Distances (VAOD/MAOD), respectively, to reconcile 4D renderings with video and the priors of multiview diffusion models; (2) Motion-Geometry Joint Alignment, which constrains known and unknown views through synchronized video and 3D inputs, ensuring consistent 4D generation; and (3) Asynchronous Optimization, which decouples Gaussian attribute and deformation network training to enhance motion and geometry fidelity. We further propose the X4D dataset, which integrates prompt, image, video, and 3D data for benchmarking. Experiments on X4D and Consistent4D demonstrate that Align4D achieves state-of-the-art quality and consistency in X-to-4D generation. Project page: https://miaoqiaowei.github.io/Align4D/.

AI.tldr: Align4D presents a flexible X-to-4D framework that converts any-modal input into coherent video-3D 4D content by aligning 4D renderings with video and multiview priors, jointly constraining motion and geometry, and decoupling optimization of attributes and deformation networks; introduces the X4D dataset and achieves state-of-the-art results on X4D and Consistent4D.
AI.motivation: Arbitrary modality-to-4D generation is hampered by the high cost of diverse training data and the limited scalability of existing methods. Leveraging video priors, multiview priors, and 3D geometry can enable coherent 4D synthesis with reduced data collection burden.
AI.method: Three core techniques: (1) Object Distance Alignment via Video-Aligned Object Distances (VAOD) and Multiview-Aligned Object Distances (MAOD) to align 4D outputs with video priors and multiview diffusion priors; (2) Motion-Geometry Joint Alignment that constrains known and unknown views through synchronized video and 3D inputs to ensure consistent 4D generation; (3) Asynchronous Optimization that decouples Gaussian attribute learning and deformation network training to improve motion and geometry fidelity. Additionally, the X4D dataset aggregates prompt, image, video, and 3D data for benchmarking.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation on X4D and Consistent4D shows Align4D achieves state-of-the-art quality and temporal/spatial consistency in X-to-4D generation.
AI.conclusion: Align4D enables flexible, scalable X-to-4D synthesis by effectively fusing video and 3D priors into 4D generation, supported by a dedicated X4D benchmark. This advances practical multimodal 4D creation, with strong results on both quality and consistency.

title: WorldDirector: Building Controllable World Simulators with Persistent Dynamic Memory
summary: We present WorldDirector, a highly controllable video world model framework designed for persistent dynamic object memory and unrestricted viewpoint exploration. Unlike existing world models that entangle physical dynamics with pixel rendering and rely on continuous visual observation to sustain motion, our framework explicitly decouples semantic motion orchestration from visual generation. By leveraging an LLM to coordinate 3D trajectories with camera movements and subsequently employing these orchestrated trajectories as control signals for video generation, our approach ensures strict physical logic and appearance stability, successfully preserving the exact visual identities of dynamic entities even when they re-enter the scene after prolonged periods out of view. Experimental results demonstrate that our method supports the synthesis of complex and extended events with unprecedented controllability and persistent dynamic object memory. Project Page: https://worlddirector.github.io/

AI.tldr: WorldDirector decouples semantic motion orchestration from visual rendering by using an LLM to plan 3D trajectories and camera moves, whose outputs guide video generation, enabling persistent dynamic object memory and precise, controllable long-horizon scenes.
AI.motivation: Current video world models entangle dynamics with rendering and rely on continuous observation, hindering memory of objects and stable identities; a separation promises strict physical consistency and flexible viewpoint control.
AI.method: A two-stage pipeline where an LLM coordinates 3D trajectories with camera trajectories; these orchestrated trajectories become control signals for the video generator, enforcing physical logic and appearance stability while preserving object identities across re-entries.
AI.result: Empirical results show the framework can synthesize complex, extended events with high controllability and persistent memory, maintaining exact visual identities of dynamic entities even after long occlusions.
AI.conclusion: WorldDirector demonstrates a viable approach to persistent, controllable video world modeling by decoupling dynamics from rendering; it enables long-horizon planning and memory, with a project page provided for further details.
